One study is here: [Geometry build performance](geometry-build/index.qmd). It
shows that SGB, SCGSim's geometry builder, derives and validates the model of
a chip with 20,000 features in 61.6 s as one serial process, that its time
grows almost linearly with the number of features, and that writing the model
directly is about 80 times faster than building it through the Gmsh API at
2,000 features. Each case ran once, on one machine.

[]{#research-and-tool-documentation}A research page gives one model's question, settings, results and
interpretation, conclusion first. What SCGSim supports in general is in
[Reference](../../reference/index.qmd), not here.

## Studies

| Study | Question | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| [Geometry build performance](geometry-build/index.qmd) | How do SGB's build time and memory grow with chip size, what does writing the model directly save over the Gmsh API, and what do the checks cost? | Random polygon layouts of up to 20,000 features, one machine, each case run once |

The setup of an older Palace Eigenmode study of a circular pad is kept under
History: [Circular Pad: study setup](../history/curved-source-installation.qmd).
It no longer applies to SCGSim 3.
